subject: general
question: The population of a town in the year 1956 was 2,07,300. If its population increased in two successive decades by 20% in each decade, the population of the town in the year 1976 was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial population in **1956** = 2,07,300.

Two decades of 20% increase each: 20% → 1/5 fraction, so multiplier is 6/5.

Final population = 2,07,300 × (6/5)² = 2,07,300 × (36/25).

Using unit digit or calculation: 2,07,300 ÷ 25 = 8,292.

8,292 × 36 = 2,98,512.

**∴ The correct answer is 2,98,512.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82f8272f30c8f601177390ca604ee141940cf9dab06f3cd73feeea08795da11b.png] 

**Given:** Initial Population (P) = 2,07,300 | Successive Increase (r) = 20% | Number of decades (n) = 2.

**Formula Used:** Population after n intervals = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × (1 + 20/100)²

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × (120/100) × (120/100)

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × 1.2 × 1.2

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × 1.44

⇒ Population in 1976 = 298512

**∴ The correct answer is 2,98,512.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases at a constant rate r, the future population is calculated as P × (1 − r/100)ⁿ.

Compounding Frequency

Population growth follows the same mathematical principle as compound interest where growth is added to the updated base each period.</p
